messages.content:
You are the Solution Architect of a platform that builds new functionality from a customer's approved specification:
business rules, screens and user stories with acceptance criteria. There is no legacy system. You design the target
service, contracts first: each use case is an operation of the REST contract the screens call. The design is hexagonal
inside: entities, ports to persistence, and use cases that implement the rules. A person approves it at gate C3 before
any code is generated.

Rules of the design:
- One bounded context (`context`, lowercase) and a base package (`base_package`, e.g. com.bank.loans).
- `entities`: the data the use cases keep, with `table` (target table, snake_case), `key` and `fields`. Every field
  has a neutral type written exactly like `decimal(19,4,signed)`, `decimal(12,2,signed)`, `integer(32,signed)`,
  `integer(64,signed)`, `text(var,40,utf8)`, `timestamp(local)`, `date(yyyy-MM-dd)` or `boolean`, and its `column`.
  Data that is only computed and returned is not an entity.
- `ports`: interfaces the domain uses to read and write data (e.g. SimulationRepository). Each method has `inputs`
  (with neutral types) and `returns`: an entity name (returned as Optional), "boolean", "int", "long" or null for
  void.
- `use_cases`: each implements a group of rules (`rules` lists their ids; every rule must be in a use case), with
  `inputs` and `outputs` named as the fields of the screens that use them, the business `errors` (a stable `code`
  like AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE and the exact `message` the specification gives), the `ports` it uses, `http_method` and
  `path` (lowercase, e.g. /simulations).
- `decisions`: the architecture decisions a reviewer must know (transactions, rounding, what is persisted).
- Names are identifiers (letters and digits, no reserved words). Leave every `legacy*` field out and `masks` empty:
  there is no legacy to compare with.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, with this shape:
{"context": "...", "base_package": "...", "entities": [{"name": "...", "table": "...", "key": ["..."],
  "fields": [{"name": "...", "type": "...", "column": "..."}]}],
 "ports": [{"name": "...", "entity": "...", "methods": [{"name": "...", "description": "...",
  "inputs": [{"name": "...", "type": "..."}], "returns": "..."}]}],
 "use_cases": [{"name": "...", "description": "...", "rules": ["RULE-001"], "inputs": [], "outputs": [],
  "errors": [{"code": "...", "message": "..."}], "ports": ["..."], "http_method": "POST", "path": "/..."}],
 "decisions": [{"title": "...", "context": "...", "decision": "...", "consequences": "..."}],
 "infrastructure": [], "masks": []}

The sequence is assigned by the persistence layer, not by the domain.","inputs":[{"name":"monto","type":"decimal(12,2,signed)"},{"name":"plazo","type":"integer(32,signed)"},{"name":"tasa_anual","type":"decimal(5,2,signed)"},{"name":"cuota_mensual","type":"decimal(12,2,signed)"},{"name":"total_pagar","type":"decimal(12,2,signed)"},{"name":"fecha_hora","type":"timestamp(local)"}],"returns":"int"}]}],"use_cases":[{"name":"SimulateLoan","description":"Simulates a consumer loan. It validates the amount (RULE-001) and the term (RULE-002), determines the annual rate from the term (RULE-003), calculates the monthly installment with the French system rounded to 2 decimals HALF_UP (RULE-004), calculates the total to pay as installment x term (RULE-005) and saves the accepted simulation with a sequential number and timestamp (RULE-006). A rejected simulation is not saved. Called by the Calcular action of SCR-SIMULADOR, whose result is shown in SCR-RESULTADO.","rules":["RULE-001","RULE-002","RULE-003","RULE-004","RULE-005","RULE-006"],"inputs":[{"name":"monto","type":"decimal(12,2,signed)"},{"name":"plazo","type":"integer(32,signed)"}],"outputs":[{"name":"tasa_anual","type":"decimal(5,2,signed)"},{"name":"cuota_mensual","type":"decimal(12,2,signed)"},{"name":"total_pagar","type":"decimal(12,2,signed)"},{"name":"numero_correlativo","type":"integer(32,signed)"}],"errors":[{"code":"AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE","message":"El monto debe estar entre 1.000 y 50.000"},{"code":"TERM_OUT_OF_RANGE","message":"El plazo debe estar entre 6 y 60 meses"}],"ports":["SimulationRepository"],"http_method":"POST","path":"/simulations"}],"decisions":[{"title":"Single operation for the whole simulation","context":"The screens call one action (Calcular) that validates, calculates and records the simulation. The rules are tightly linked: the rate feeds the installment, the installment feeds the total, and all of them feed the saved record.","decision":"One use case, SimulateLoan, exposed as POST /simulations, implements RULE-001 to RULE-006. Calculation stays in pure domain code with no dependency on persistence. Only the save goes through the SimulationRepository port.","consequences":"The UI makes a single call and gets tasa_anual, cuota_mensual and total_pagar. Business errors are returned as a 422 response with the stable code and the exact message from the specification."},{"title":"Validation order and rejection without side effects","context":"Both the amount and the term can be invalid at once, and the screen shows a single error message (mensaje_error). A rejected simulation must not be saved (RULE-006).","decision":"The amount is validated first (AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE), then the term (TERM_OUT_OF_RANGE). The range limits are inclusive: 1000.00 to 50000.00 and 6 to 60. Validation runs before any calculation or port call, so a rejection never touches the repository.","consequences":"A rejected request leaves no record. If both values are invalid, only the amount message is returned."},{"title":"Rounding and numeric precision","context":"The installment follows the French formula M x i / (1 - (1+i)^-n) with i = tasa_anual / 100 / 12. The specification requires 2 decimals with rounding half up. Examples: 10000.00 at 12.00 for 12 months gives 888.49; 5000.00 at 14.50 for 24 months gives 241.25.","decision":"All money and rate arithmetic uses BigDecimal, never floating point. The intermediate steps (i, (1+i)^-n) use a high-precision MathContext (at least 20 digits). Only the final installment is rounded, to scale 2 with RoundingMode.HALF_UP. The total is the already rounded installment multiplied by the term, kept at scale 2 (888.49 x 12 = 10661.88). The rate comes from fixed bands: term <= 12 gives 12.00, 13 to 36 gives 14.50, 37 to 60 gives 16.00.","consequences":"Results are deterministic and match the approved acceptance scenarios. The total can differ from monto plus interest by a few cents because it is based on the rounded installment, as the rule states."},{"title":"Persistence of accepted simulations for audit","context":"RULE-006 requires each accepted simulation to be stored with a sequential number, amount, term, rate, installment, total and date/time.","decision":"The accepted simulation is saved in table simulation. numero_correlativo is generated by the database (identity or sequence) and returned by SimulationRepository.save. fecha_hora is taken from an injectable Clock in the domain, so it can be tested. The calculation and the save run in one transaction.","consequences":"If the save fails, no result is returned and nothing is stored. Records are insert-only; no update or delete operations are defined."}],"infrastructure":[],"masks":[]}
